correctness.rationale: The finite-sum/tail identity and derivative-elimination identity hold algebraically. Strictly decreasing exact binomial convolution ratios plus Descartes bound positive y-roots after z=-1-y; endpoint signs and the variational root equation prove counts and uniqueness. Analytic pointwise convergence of R_N gives the sharp limit. SymPy checker independently tests 413 exact/symbolic instances; the infinite claim is based on proof, not tests.

evidence: Edholm–Mathew gives effective Bergman-kernel formulas and rational oblique slices, while Deng–Fu proves positive unit-circle values of a palindromic rational-Hartogs numerator; neither gives this vertex polynomial real-root phase diagram.
Fu gives the number of bounded near-vertex zeros and possible multiple-zero type, not their real-versus-complex count by every degree and parameter.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The stronger kernel existence/total-zero theorems do not imply this location statistic, and the diagonal numerator is a distinct parameter-dependent polynomial. Existing real double-root splitting in the limiting exceptional case is credited as prior.

evidence: Fu establishes at most one double negative root, necessarily odd N and alpha below 1/2, not one collision for EVERY odd N; provides no parameter threshold converging to 1/2.
For each even N, Fu does not provide the exact one-negative-real-root statement.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Being allowed a possible repeated root is strictly weaker than proving that a unique parameter yields it for every odd degree, with the full two/one/zero real-count diagram. The present Descartes/TP2 coefficient proof supplies this missing implication.

evidence: Fu writes exactly P_delta(z)/delta=Q_{N,alpha}(z), proves that there is at most one double negative zero and all other zeros are simple, and gives N=3 critical alpha; Sections 3 and 5 do not state an all-N negative-real zero count or unique collision threshold.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The exact same polynomial and its normalization were deliberately matched. The existing lemma on possible multiplicity does not imply existence/uniqueness of a collision for each odd N, one real zero in each even N, or the threshold limit.

evidence: A degree-three discriminant and critical value are already explicitly recorded by Fu; not claimed as novel. No all-degree phase table was identified in the inspected primary sources.
exact_database_or_table.reasoning: The new result is the complete all-degree classification; matching a low-degree table entry cannot imply this. Search absence is not uniqueness proof.

originality.rationale: Compared the identical polynomial and its known double-root lemma in Qian Fu, with full relevant manuscript read. That work does not imply the all-degree parity counting law, universal existence and uniqueness of odd collision thresholds, or their 1/2 limit; other inspected Hartogs numerator papers work with different slices. Risk remains of an older equivalent result.
residual_risks: Older literature on partial sums of arithmetic–geometric series or truncated power sums could give an equivalent all-degree root-location classification.
The 2026-11-11 Fu manuscript is very close in object and proves key prior lemmas; distinctions must be maintained in any publication.

value.rationale: The sign and location of zero fibres in generalized Hartogs vertex sections depend on whether the finite polynomial zeros are real. A complete natural all-degree parity classification and unique collision threshold with asymptotic value provide a meaningful missing analytic kernel invariant, not a tiny arbitrary finite table or elementary renaming.
